where: the 'If the kiosk still waits' list on the rail-less counselor page (identical in kiosk-menu-counselor)
finding: The block that just became this role's whole reference is the only prose on the page with no measure. Every other text object here — the lede, the ten-minute hint, both footnotes — wraps at the same capped measure, so the page has one clean right ragged edge; the list ignores it and runs to the column edge, setting 12px type at about a hundred characters a line and overhanging the paragraph directly beneath it by 120px. It reads as the one block that was pasted in rather than set, and it is the block a counselor at 6:40pm is meant to skim: the longest lines on the page, in the smallest type, at the moment with the least patience. On the admin build the same markup is invisible because the 448px column crops it, which is what makes it an oversight rather than a choice.
evidence: kiosk-setup-counselor--desktop: the second list item runs x=416–1019 (603px) while both footer paragraphs below stop at x=898 (482px) and the lede at x=988. The `ul` is `flex flex-col gap-2 text-xs leading-relaxed text-ink-400` with no `max-w-prose`; every sibling paragraph on the page carries one.
direction: Give the list the measure the rest of the register already keeps, so the page has one right edge and the reference reads at the same length as the small print under it. The cap belongs on the block, not on the column, or it will come back the next time this section is given room.

where: the qualifying sentence above the 'If the kiosk still waits' list in the right column
finding: The new line is meant to demote the three causes beneath it, and it is set below them. It sits at exactly the value of the uppercase heading above it and a full step darker than the list it introduces, so the ranking runs backwards: the three reasons that are not in force arrive at the register's ordinary body weight, and the sentence saying they are not in force is the faintest object in the column. A qualifier read after the thing it qualifies does not qualify it — the reader takes on three false causes first and the correction second, on the one frame where a cause is already named on the left.
evidence: kiosk-setup-denied--desktop: 'Once the role is granted…' at y=383–408 peaks at luminance 114, the same value as the 'IF THE KIOSK STILL WAITS' heading; the three list items below peak at 161. The line is `text-ink-500`, the list `text-ink-400`, both 12px leading-relaxed.
direction: Let the demotion run downhill. Either the qualifier takes the register's ordinary body rank and the list steps under it, or it binds to the heading as a deck and the list is unmistakably subordinate to both — but the sentence that says 'not these, not yet' cannot be the quietest thing in its own column.

where: the two columns of the register below the rule — the interval between each uppercase heading and the first thing under it (same in kiosk-menu and kiosk-setup-denied)
finding: The grid now sets two columns as peers and their headings on one line, and then the two columns space themselves by different systems, so nothing after the headings agrees. In the left column the heading is 12px from its first line — which is also the interval between the verdict group and the buttons, and between the buttons and the facts — so 'This deployment' binds to its section no more tightly than the section's own parts bind to each other; it floats at the top of an evenly spaced run. In the right column the heading is 8px from its list and 24px from the next section, which is the correct binding. The visible cost is small and constant: the row's shared top edge survives the headings and breaks on the first body line, 5px apart across a 32px gutter, which is exactly the distance at which a misalignment reads as a slip rather than a stagger.
evidence: kiosk-setup--desktop: both h2s occupy y=308–316; the left column's first body line caps at y=337, the right column's at y=332. Left section is `flex flex-col gap-3` with h2, verdict group, action group and dl as equal siblings; the right sections are `flex flex-col gap-2` inside a `gap-6` stack.
direction: Fix one heading-to-body interval for the whole register and make it the tightest gap in either column, so a heading always belongs to what follows it; the left column's grouping intervals should then be larger than that, not equal to it. The columns' first lines will land together as a consequence rather than as a separate correction.

where: the role badge and 'Sign out' on one line in the account popover's identity block (same on the admin build in kiosk-menu)
finding: The exit's new position glues it to an inert label. The role badge is a filled, rounded box, and it now sits 8px from the sign-out control — closer than any other pair of objects in the panel — so at a glance the two read as one segmented control rather than a fact and an action. It is worse under a pointer, where the sign-out button's hover surface is the same fill and radius the badge is wearing at rest: hovering the exit produces a second identical box beside the first, and the badge spends the whole time looking like the half of it you have not moved to yet. This is the one place on a navigation surface where something inert dresses as pressable.
evidence: kiosk-menu-counselor--desktop: `counselor` at 8px (`gap-2`) from ``. Every other interval in the panel is 12px or more.
direction: Keep the exit where the reach argument put it and break the pairing instead — either open the distance so the badge and the control are plainly two different species, or let the role read as a label rather than as a filled chip, so nothing in the identity block wears the exit's hover surface while doing nothing.
